title: Hummer H2
verdict: GM took a Suburban frame, cut seven inches out of the middle and wrapped it in Hummer-shaped bodywork. Purists called it a costume. It turned out to be a full-time 4WD truck with a rear locker and 35s from the factory, and it handles a rough trail better than most of the people who bought it ever found out.

paragraphs: The H2 is what happened when General Motors bought the most famous name in off-roading and decided it should sell in volume. AM General built it under contract in a new plant in Mishawaka, Indiana, but GM engineered it from its own truck parts: a shortened Suburban frame, a three-quarter-ton front end and a 6.0-liter small-block V8. It went on sale as a 2003 model for less than half the price of an [[hummer/h1|H1]]. Car and Driver took one 2,000 miles through Baja and decided it was 'not a Hummer poseur'. It was something else, and that's mostly fine.

story.heading: FROM SHOW CAR TO SUBURBAN FRAME
paragraphs: In December 1999 GM bought the rights to the Hummer name from AM General, and the H2 was the first product of that deal. GM showed an H2 concept in 2000 with independent rear suspension, then priced it out of the production truck. Wikipedia credits the design to Clay Dean; the Chicago Tribune named Terry Henline as chief designer when the pickup concept appeared at the 2001 New York show. GM's 2003 spec sheet named the H2's rivals as the [[range-rover/l322|Range Rover]], the [[lexus/lx470|Lexus LX 470]] and the Lincoln Navigator, so luxury buyers were the target from the start.

The production recipe was pure GM parts bin. Engineers took a Suburban frame, cut 7.2 inches out of its middle for a 122.8-inch wheelbase and trimmed the overhangs, giving a truck nine inches shorter than a Tahoe. The torsion-bar front suspension came from a 2500-series Suburban, the rear became a five-link live axle on coils, and GM said a diesel wouldn't package. The radiator support and engine box are welded to the body, so the big front-hinged hood doesn't shimmy against the rest of the truck.

story.heading: WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES IN THE DIRT
paragraphs: Under the costume is a serious drivetrain. A full-time BorgWarner 44-84 transfer case sends 60 percent of the torque to the rear, locks 50/50 at any speed and has a 2.64:1 low range. The 4.10 rear axle carries an Eaton ELocker that engages only in 4LO below 20 mph. Bosch ABS and traction control are tuned for rough ground, and skid plates cover the engine, transfer case and fuel tank. The front chin plate has 'H2' embossed on it, because of course it does.

GM's figures give the coil-sprung truck a 40.4-degree approach and a 39.6-degree departure angle, and the off-road package's LT315/70R17s push the approach to 43.6 degrees. Ground clearance is about ten inches against the H1's sixteen, so in Baja Car and Driver learned to put a tire on the rock rather than straddle it. The optional rear air suspension can lift the tail about two inches and runs an air hose for the tires. The H1's central tire inflation wouldn't work with GM's axles.

story.heading: THE PICKUP, THE 6.2 AND THE END
paragraphs: The SUT arrived for 2005: an H2 with a short bed and an Avalanche-style Midgate that folds to open the cabin into the bed. US sales peaked at 34,529 in 2003 and slid as fuel prices rose. For 2008 GM gave the H2 a new interior, a 393-hp aluminum 6.2-liter V8 and the six-speed 6L80. Towing went from 6,500 to 8,000 pounds and the crawl ratio rose to about 39:1. Owners rate those last trucks the best H2s, and they're the hardest to find.

The timing couldn't have been worse. GM put Hummer up for sale in 2008, and a deal with China's Tengzhong collapsed in February 2010. H2 production ended in 2009. Avtotor in Kaliningrad, Russia, had also assembled H2s from 2006 to 2009. GM's US sales figures add up to 153,026 H2s. The Mishawaka plant was sold in 2017 to SF Motors, a maker of electric vehicles.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · THE 8,500-POUND LOOPHOLE
callout.title: Why there's no EPA sticker
paragraphs: The H2's gross vehicle weight rating is 8,600 pounds. Until 2011 the EPA exempted vehicles over 8,500 pounds GVWR from fuel-economy testing and standards, so GM never had to publish a rating, and H2s didn't count toward its fleet average.

Magazines measured it themselves. Car and Driver and Motor Trend both recorded about 10 mpg, Edmunds 9.2 and Four Wheeler 10.8. With a 32-gallon tank, H2 owners on 37s still stop for fuel 'long before I need to pee', as one forum owner put it.

engineering_intro: The H2 sits on a modified GMT820 ladder frame: a GM three-quarter-ton front section and a shortened half-ton Suburban rear. It has torsion-bar independent front suspension, a five-link coil-sprung rear axle with an optional air-spring rear, and full-time 4WD through a BorgWarner 44-84 transfer case. The 6.0-liter LQ4 and four-speed 4L65-E powered it through 2007, then the 6.2-liter L92 and six-speed 6L80 for 2008–09. Wheels are 8-lug, 8 x 165.1 mm.

engineering.v: Shortened Suburban ladder frame, 122.8 in wheelbase
engineering.note: Car and Driver: 7.2 in cut from the middle. Wikipedia describes a modified GMT820 three-quarter-ton front with a half-ton rear section.
Control arms and torsion bars from the 2500-series Suburban. Ride height is adjusted at the torsion-bar keys.

engineering.v: Five-link live axle, coils or air springs
engineering.note: Optional self-leveling rear air springs (RPO ZM6) lift the tail about 2 in. The rear axle is an AAM 9.5-inch 14-bolt semi-float, according to owners.
40/60 front/rear split, 2.64:1 low range. Modes: 4HI, 4HI Lock, 4LO Lock and Neutral for flat towing.
Works only in 4LO Lock and disengages above 20 mph. Brake-based traction control handles the front axle.
The LQ4 made about 315–325 hp. The aluminum-block L92, with variable valve timing, made 393 hp and 415 lb-ft.

generations_table.note: Four-speed 4L65-E, 4.10 axles, LT315/70R17 tires on GM's spec sheet. The rear air suspension came with the Adventure package.
Re-rated engine, same four-speed. Owners say the front diff and build quality improved from mid-2005.
Short bed, Midgate and an outside swing-away spare. Car and Driver priced a test truck at $52,845.
Six-speed 6L80, new interior, 8,000 lb towing, crawl ratio about 39:1, stronger transfer case, quicker steering. Lower bumpers painted silver.

buying_checks.head: Find out what the air suspension has been doing
buying_checks.body: If the rear compressor runs at every stop light, there's a leak somewhere and the compressor is cooking itself. One owner was quoted $2,250 for a GM compressor before labor. Many trucks have already been converted to coils, which owners say costs under $250 in parts. Check which you're buying and whether the onboard air hose still works.

buying_checks.head: Shake the front end
buying_checks.body: 35-inch tires wear out ball joints, tie rods, pitman and idler arms and hub bearings, even in normal driving. Owners list the front ball joints and tie-rod ends as weak points. Budget roughly $400 in parts for a front-end rebuild before labor, and more if the torsion bars have been cranked.

buying_checks.head: Listen for a clunk from the front diff
buying_checks.body: The front differential hangs on three rubber bushings that soften with age, oil and coolant leaks. A loose diff clunks over bumps. Owners replace them with Outfitter Design's UHMW kit; one paid $400 to have it installed.

buying_checks.head: Cycle every 4WD mode
buying_checks.body: Shift through 4HI, 4HI Lock and 4LO Lock, and lock the rear diff in 4LO. A SERVICE 4WD message or a slow shift points to the encoder motor, the dash buttons or wiring. A bang followed by no 4WD at all usually means the plastic shift fork inside the transfer case has broken.

buying_checks.head: Look up at the roof and the sunroof
buying_checks.body: Owners keep naming water leaks from the roof clearance lights and the sunroof. Check the headliner, the carpet and the rear cargo area for stains or a musty smell.

buying_checks.head: Know which truck you want
buying_checks.body: 2008–09 trucks have the 6.2, the six-speed and a far better interior, and owners say they're better 'in every way'. They also use some parts specific to those years, and 2009s are rare. 2003–07 trucks are cheaper and have more junkyard parts. Owners call the 4L65-E four-speed the drivetrain's weak link.

buying_checks.head: Inspect the chassis, not the chrome
buying_checks.body: Dealers can detail out a lot, but not rock gouges in the frame and skid plates. Lifts, tires and wiring added by previous owners are common, so trace any extra switches or lights, and run the VIN for open recalls.

repairs.title: Front differential bushings
repairs.time: ≈ Half a day (much less if the diff is already out for gears)
repairs.cost: One owner: $400 to install, about $600 all in with the kit
repairs.symptoms: A clunk from the front over bumps, or the diff visibly rocking when someone shifts between Park, Reverse and Drive. Oil or coolant dripping onto the old rubber bushings speeds up the wear.
repairs.fix: Support the front diff, disconnect the front driveshaft and CV axles as needed, and unbolt the three mounts: the crossmember bushing, the top mount and the side mount. Press out the old rubber and fit all three replacement bushings, since Outfitter Design sells them only as a kit so the mounts share the same hardness. Fix the oil leaks first if you can; one shop wouldn't install new bushings until the leaks were repaired.
repairs.tools: Jack and transmission or diff jack · press or bushing tools · torque wrench. Outfitter Design's kit is UHMW (one crossmember bushing plus top and side mount bushings with steel sleeves).

parts.name: H2 front differential bushing kit (UHMW, all three mounts)

repairs.title: Rear air suspension: compressor, air springs or coil conversion
repairs.cost: One owner was quoted $2,250 for a GM compressor before labor; another converted to coils for under $250 in parts
repairs.symptoms: SERVICE AIR SUSPENSION message, the rear sagging overnight, or a compressor that runs constantly. The owner's manual says leveling pauses with any door open, so close everything before you diagnose it.
repairs.fix: To repair it, find the leak first (lines, fittings or the air springs) before replacing the compressor. Owners say later dual-stage compressors are less likely to overheat, and switching to one needs two new hoses. To convert, support the frame, lower the axle (one owner didn't need to remove the shocks), remove the air springs and fit coil springs with upper and lower isolators.
repairs.tools: Jack and stands · basic sockets · soapy water for leak checks. Fabtech lists H2 coil-spring and air-bag lift options.

parts.name: H2 2003–09 OEM air bag lift parts

repairs.title: Steering linkage rebuild: tie rods, pitman arm, idler arm and support
repairs.time: ≈ Half a day plus an alignment
repairs.cost: About $400 in parts for one owner's front end, not including shocks
repairs.symptoms: Wander, a steering wheel that won't center, clunks over bumps and uneven tire wear. Lifted trucks and cranked torsion bars make it worse: one owner says parts wore out 'five times faster'.
repairs.fix: Separate the tie-rod ends, pitman arm and idler arm with a puller, count the turns on the tie-rod sleeves to keep a rough toe setting, and replace the worn parts. Owners recommend heavier tie rods and an idler and pitman support kit if you run 37s. Grease every fitting afterwards. The idler support's fitting can't be reached without removing it, so a grease-relocation kit helps. Get the truck aligned.
repairs.tools: Pitman arm puller · tie-rod separator · grease gun · torque wrench. The H2 shares its steering with 2001–10 GM HD trucks.

parts.name: Kryptonite Death Grip idler support (fits Hummer H2)
Forged pitman/idler arm support kit, 2001–10 GM 2500/3500 (confirm H2 fit)

repairs.title: Front lower ball joints
repairs.time: ≈ 3–6 hours (one shop quoted 6 hours for both sides)
repairs.cost: $720 with parts at one shop; ball joints $20–40 each for a DIYer
repairs.symptoms: An alignment that won't hold, play at the bottom of the knuckle when you rock the tire top to bottom, and clunks. In one owner's 2006 the upper ball joint pulled out of the control arm while driving.
repairs.fix: Unload the torsion bar first. Then remove the wheel, brake caliper and rotor, separate the lower ball joint from the knuckle, and press the old joint out of the control arm with a rented ball-joint press. One owner needed a torch and 'a lot of patience' with a breaker bar. Press in the new joint, torque it, grease it (the manual says not below 10°F) and get an alignment.
repairs.tools: Ball-joint press (rentable) · torsion-bar unloading tool · torch · breaker bar · torque wrench.

repairs.title: Front wheel hub bearing
repairs.symptoms: A growl that changes with speed or when you weave, play at the wheel, or ABS, traction control and SERVICE 4WD warnings when a failing hub damages the wheel-speed sensor. One owner running 37s is on their sixth set.
repairs.fix: Remove the wheel, caliper, rotor and CV axle nut, unplug the ABS sensor, then unbolt the hub from the knuckle and fit the new unit. Owners prefer Timken, which they say is the OE supplier, or the ACDelco FW314. Torque the axle nut to the factory figure; owners disagree about the number, so check the service manual.
repairs.tools: Large axle-nut socket · breaker bar · hub puller or a hammer for seized hubs · torque wrench.

repairs.title: Transfer case won't shift: encoder motor or shift fork
repairs.time: ≈ 1 hour for the motor, an afternoon to drop the case for a fork
repairs.cost: Owners quote about $200–400 for an encoder motor
repairs.symptoms: A SERVICE 4WD message, mode lights that keep flashing, shifts that take minutes, or a bang followed by no 4HI or 4LO at all.
repairs.fix: Scan the codes first. Clean or check the dash buttons, then check the encoder motor on the transfer case and its wiring. Owners warn that remanufactured and non-OEM motors are 'rubbish'. One owner says the usual failure is the contact ring inside the encoder, sold separately. If the case banged and stopped working, the plastic shift fork has probably broken: drop the transfer case, fit an aluminum fork and refill with fresh fluid.
repairs.tools: Scan tool that reads transfer-case codes · transmission jack · seal kit · fluid pump.

repairs.title: Radiator replacement
repairs.symptoms: A coolant puddle at the front, a crack in a plastic tank, rising temperatures when towing.
repairs.fix: Drain the coolant, then disconnect the hoses and the transmission cooler lines. Their retention clips are the worst part of the job, and one owner drove for a month with a clip not fully seated. Lift the radiator out without bending the fins; the front-hinged hood makes this awkward alone. Replace the lower hose while you're there, then refill with DEX-COOL and bleed the system.
repairs.tools: Drain pan · trans-line clip tool · something solid to stand on in the engine bay.

repairs.title: Heater core quick-connect leak
repairs.cost: A fitting and a coolant top-up
repairs.symptoms: Coolant running down the passenger side of the transmission bell housing while the passenger floor stays dry, and the engine running warm with the heater on.
repairs.fix: Before you condemn the heater core, check the quick-connect fittings at the core. Slide a release tool of the right size up into the fitting to free the clips, twist the fitting off, fit the new one, push the hose on, refit the clip and top up the coolant.

baseline_service.intro: Most H2s are now 17 to 23 years old, and few were serviced off-road. Treat every gear oil as unknown. The rear diff carries the E-locker, the transfer case is easy to neglect, and the front end needs grease. Fluids changed in 2008: the owner's manual lists DEXRON-III for the transmission and transfer case on a 2004, and DEXRON-VI on a 2008.

items.spec: SAE 5W-30 meeting GM6094M · 6.0 qt (5.7 L) with filter
items.interval: When the oil-life monitor says so, and at least once a year
items.note: The 2004 manual lists the ACDelco PF44 filter (GM 25010633). The 2008 manual lists the PF48 (GM 89017524).

items.spec: GM 88944151 (2004 manual) · ACDelco A2948C / GM 10389652 (2008 manual)
items.interval: Inspect at every oil change; replace per the manual's schedule
items.note: Dusty trails clog it quickly. Check it after any desert trip.

items.interval: Per the owner's manual schedule [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]; do them now if there are no receipts
items.note: The same plug is listed for the 6.0 and the 6.2. Inspect the wires when you change the plugs, as the manual says.

items.spec: DEX-COOL 50/50 · 13.0 qt (2004 manual); 16.7 qt SUV / 15.4 qt SUT (2008 manual)
items.note: The manual warns that other coolants can corrode the radiator and heater core. One forum owner changes it every three years to protect the aluminum.

items.spec: DEXRON-III (4L65-E, 2003–07) · DEXRON-VI (6L80, 2008–09) · 6.0 qt with pan removal and filter (2008 manual)
items.interval: Fluid and filter on the severe-service schedule if you tow, run hills or sit in hot traffic
items.note: Do a pan drop and filter change rather than a flush. Owners call the four-speed the weak link, so treat its fluid as cheap insurance.

items.spec: DEXRON-III (2004 manual) · DEXRON-VI (2008 manual) · 1.5 qt (1.4 L)
items.interval: Per the manual's mileage schedule; more often if you wade or tow
items.note: Fill to just below the fill hole. The manual also says to check that the transfer-case vent hose isn't kinked. Loosen the fill plug before you open the drain.

items.spec: SAE 75W-90 synthetic meeting GM 9986115 (GM 12378261 in the 2004 manual, 89021677 in 2008)
items.interval: At purchase, then after any deep water crossing
items.note: Owners report the front takes about 2 quarts and the rear about 3. Many run Mobil 1 75W-90 synthetic. A forum owner warns that conventional 85W-90 can make the front diff stick and dart on cold mornings.

Grease the front suspension, ball joints and steering linkage, but not the ball joints below 10°F (-12°C), per the manual. Dealers don't always do it: one was told the joints were sealed. The front propshaft spline takes GM spline lubricant 12345879.

items.interval: Check at every oil change; flush if dark
items.note: The H2 uses Hydro-boost brakes, so the power steering pump also powers the brake booster. NHTSA's 05V455000 recall notes that losing steering fluid can also mean losing power brakes.

items.interval: Flush at purchase if there's no record
items.note: A 6,400-pound truck on big tires needs good brakes. Car and Driver measured 244 ft from 70 mph on a stock 2003.

items.spec: ACDelco GF626 (GM 25121792) in the 2004 manual's parts list
items.interval: At purchase if there's no record [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: The 2008 manual's maintenance parts list doesn't include a separate fuel filter, so check whether your year has one.

items.spec: Serpentine belt; inspect the cooling hoses
items.interval: Inspect per the manual's schedule; replace when cracked
items.note: The manual recommends a yearly pressure test of the cooling system and cap.

items.spec: Compressor, two height sensors, two air springs
items.note: Listen for the compressor running constantly and look for a rear that sags overnight, both signs of a leak. The owner's manual says leveling stops with any door open.

A weak battery causes odd 4WD and electrical faults, and the rear locker disengages when battery voltage is low (owner's manual). Owners say other group sizes fit if you leave out the plastic battery box.

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: Owners agree on 37x12.50R17 on stock wheels, or wheels with the same offset. One owner runs Cooper STTs at stock height with a slight torsion-bar crank and doesn't rub at full stuff, apart from a light scrub on the sway bar at full lock, which the stock 35s do too. 37x14.50s didn't fit. Wider tires or different offsets need a lift, spacers or both.

faq.q: Is it really just a Tahoe underneath?
faq.a: Partly. Car and Driver reported a Suburban frame cut down by 7.2 inches, a 2500-series front suspension and a Suburban five-link rear. The body, transfer-case calibration, rear E-locker, skid plates and angles are H2-specific, and AM General built the trucks in Mishawaka. Parts for the engine and front end cross over with GM trucks; body and trim parts mostly don't.

faq.q: What fuel economy does it get?
faq.a: No official rating exists, because its 8,600-lb GVWR exempted it from EPA testing. Magazines measured 9 to 10.8 mpg. Owners on 37s report about 10.5 mpg on the stock 4.10 gears, and one got 12.5 after regearing to 4.56.

Every H2 has a lockable center differential and an Eaton ELocker in the rear axle. The rear locker only works in 4LO Lock, engages below 2 mph and drops out above 20 mph. There's no front locker from the factory; one owner added an Eaton E-locker to the front diff while regearing.

If budget allows, 2008–09 for the 6.2, the six-speed and the much better interior; owners say they're better in every way. They're also the rarest and most expensive, and some of their parts are specific to those years. Among 2003–07 trucks, one owner would pick a mid-2005 to 2007 truck over a 2003 for the stronger front diff and better build.

faq.q: Should I keep the air suspension?
faq.a: Opinion is split. Owners who tow love being able to raise and lower the rear, and the onboard air hose. Others have replaced compressors more than once at around $2,000 installed and switched to coils, saying the ride hardly changed. If the compressor runs constantly, find the leak before replacing it.
GM's 2003 spec sheet said 7,000 lb. GM's 2008 announcement said the new powertrain raised capacity from 6,500 to 8,000 lb. Use tow/haul mode, and check your door sticker and hitch rating.

faq.q: Do I need to regear for 37s?
faq.a: Owners say the stock 4.10s with 37s feel gutless on the highway and the transmission keeps hunting for gears. 4.56 restores roughly stock feel on 37s; 4.88 suits 38s or bigger and towing. Expect to retune the speedometer and shift points afterwards. Owners were quoted $1,900 to $4,800 for both axles.

faq.q: Can I level it with the torsion bars?
faq.a: Yes. Crank the stock keys or fit GM's re-indexed 'green' keys; one owner gained about an inch with the green keys alone. Owners warn that cranked torsion bars ride harsher and wear tie rods, pitman and idler arms much faster, and the extra height leaves a gap above the bump stops.

The transfer-case control system has a fault. Common causes are sticking dash buttons or a mode dial, a failing encoder motor on the transfer case, damaged wiring, or a bad wheel-speed sensor or hub bearing. Have it scanned with a proper tool, because a cheap code reader won't show the module's codes.

faq.q: How do I flat-tow it behind an RV?
faq.a: The transfer case has a NEUTRAL position for towing the H2 with all four wheels on the ground; the owner's manual explains the procedure. Set the parking brake before you select NEUTRAL, because the truck can roll even with the transmission in Park.

mods.why: The H2 sits nose-down from the factory. A leveling kit or torsion-bar keys raise the front for 37s. Owners run 40s on 6-inch lifts with 4.5-inch-backspace wheels, but suspension lifts drop the torsion bars and crossmember lower under the truck.
35s and 37s eat the stock linkage and ball joints. Heavier tie rods, a pitman and idler support and better ball joints are the usual first spend.

who.name: Kryptonite — upper control arms (2001–10 GM HD)

mods.why: Solid UHMW bushings stop the front diff rocking in its mounts, and owners say the front end feels 'ten years newer' after the swap.

who.name: Outfitter Design — H2 front differential bushing kit

mods.why: Regear to 4.56 for 37s or 4.88 for 38s and up, and add a front locker while the diff is apart. Retune the computer afterwards.

who.name: RockAuto — H2 ring & pinion and install kits

mods.why: One owner says a stock-height H2 'hits everything on the trail with the front skid'. Steel bumpers and sliders take the abuse instead, and leveling the truck helps.
